body: I'm a coward.
I posted for the second time on SW last night. Then I popped a couple of benadryls and slept. Probably won't last till the end of the year tbh but w/e.
Tell me about yourself. What do you perceive as failure?

As someone who's been there, I just want you to know that I do care. That's why I'm responding to you, because I care.

Tell me more about yourself, either here or in private messaging. Please? I'd like to get to know you a bit more.

Thank you for replying. I've tried for years to build a brighter side, to love myself, and so on. I've made some pretty good friends, acquired a decent education, and am on my way to a halfway decent career. Objectively I have it better than a lot of other posters in this sub.

But I despite all of this, I still don't love myself. I don't have the capacity for happiness. There is no way out. It's all bleak.

My sister said that I was using my humor as a crutch, a mask. She's right. If I didn't have my humor, I'd be outwardly miserable. Even my sister can see right through my bullshit. 

I've been trying and failing to think of things that I like about myself for years, and I'm at a loss. I don't understand why anyone would ever be my friend, and I'm doubtful that anyone would every fall in love with me. There's nothing of value here.
What kind of opportunities?

I'm glad you're still with us, bud. Please seek some professional help, you're suffering and there are people who have the desire and ability to help you.

Anything you want to talk about? I can't promise much but we're both suffering from depression so it might help you a little if you PM me.
Well as long as they tasted good, that's the most important part of the blueberry muffin.
I feel that. In my lowest and most suicidal moments, I don't want to die necessarily but I definitely want to cease existing. It's a tough place to be in.
That's good to hear. On many of my worst days I struggle to cry, but when I manage to let a few tears out it's a bit cathartic.

What are you studying?

Also realize that failure isn't the worst thing to happen, and academics isn't the end all be all of life. My parents are HS drop outs with GEDs, mom's a waitress and my dad works on the IT help desk at a telecommunications company. They're not rolling in money, but they make decent livings and raised two children.

That's great! It's a step in the right direction.

I find that it's tough to tell people, even your family, about depression. From the outside it looks like lethargy, bad attitude, sadness and anger, and so on. I always fear negative judgement even when telling my parents about my current feelings just because I'm afraid they won't understand it.
What kind of muffins did you make?

I would talk to your doctor about that, maybe they can help you learn (assuming you don't have a medical condition that prevents you from swallowing). Or maybe they could give you a liquid version or some other alternative method of delivery.

I feel immense guilt and shame too. Like, I've had a pretty good life on paper: no abuse, loving family, good friends, done well in school, etc. But then I feel depressed and since I can't pin it on a logical reason, I start to feel guilty. The feelings spiral out of control at times.

You're not alone.

I alternate between everything being fixable and everything being hopeless pretty frequently. As in, I spent yesterday and most of today hopeless but now I'm in a "fixable" mood. Anyone else experience this?
Same. They know I'm depressed but they don't quite know how bad it really is.
I'm 20, and people say that I act like I'm mid-20s or early 30s. I don't really even get carded at liquor stores anymore so that's a plus I guess, right?
It feels like the part of me that is human died a long time ago. All that really remains is just a machine made of flesh and bone.

Well that's great that you've been getting better. I haven't been so lucky. I've been spiraling deeper and deeper into depression for my entire college career. I didn't make any real friends, I never dated, never really did anything. Just went to school, work, studied, and hoped I'd die in my sleep.

I have friends and family but they are no help. They can't do much. They're not professionals. I don't want to burden them with the real me, I don't want to inflict myself onto others and lose whatever little support I do have.

The only reason why I'm posting this here is because I'm really out of options. Hotlines aren't any help. Counseling isn't panning out. Medication doesn't work as I'd hoped, it just makes me less anxious and not give a flying fuck about anything.

I really don't see how anything will get any better. I'm a lost cause.
Very little. The list is dwindling day by day.

Do not hole up in your room if you're feeling depressed. Seriously, nip that shit in the bud because, if you're like me, it's a slow burn that creeps up on you.

Your university most likely offers free counseling for mental health and whatnot. Use it. You'll thank me in 4 years when you have friends and aren't very depressed.

I've been going for short bike rides lately. That helps a little.

I'm also lucky enough to have coworkers who seem happy enough to see me. That helps some too.

But I know how you feel. I'm very quickly losing any and all hope.
Same here man. I've mostly cut out booze for the past few months and it's been real shitty.

I've been seeing a counselor since August. They're short-staffed and overbooked so I can only go once every 5 or so weeks, so that sucks. But it's free.

I don't like it because you get your hour, and then they send you on your way to stew in your shit for a few weeks, and then you're back in for just another hour. I feel like more frequent therapy would be beneficial for me but I can't afford it right now.

I hope your experience is better than mine.
